newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end up on widespread buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end up on widespread buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Thursday, buoyed by widespread local and foreign buying of blue chips, brokers said.
The Colombo all share index closed 10.8 points higher at 787.4, maintaining this week's steady rise.
"Foreigners were very active in blue chips. Other speculative shares were also active," said Prasanna Chandrasekera of John Keells brokers.
He said foreigners have been enthused by earnings forecasts for blue chips, most of which are likely to perform better this year.
Chandrasekera said the market was also boosted by Cold Stores' announcement of a one for two bonus issue. Its share rose 16 rupees to 205.

Turnover was sharply higher at over 330 million rupees, led mainly by nearly 800,000 shares of DFCC. "There was lot of activity in the market. While foreign funds were aiming for blue chips, retailers were looking for speculative shares for short-term gains," said a broker with Lanka Securities
Lanka Orix was up 10 rupees at 230, Sampath Bank was up 2.75 rupees at 73 and Tea Smallholders rose 4.75 to 64 rupees. The market will be closed on Friday for a Buddhist holiday.
